root_cause.defect: RuntimeRobotsPolicy (packages/research-local/src/opintel_research_local/robots.py) does not honor the HTTP Content-Encoding of the robots.txt response. _retrieve() passes transport.request(...).body straight through, and evaluate() calls body.decode('utf-8', errors='strict') on it. When the origin/CDN serves robots.txt gzip-compressed (Cloudflare default), the raw gzip bytes raise UnicodeDecodeError -> caught -> reason_code 'robots_malformed' -> allowed stays False -> decision DENY -> M1 fails closed.
root_cause.contrast: The page-fetch path SafeHttpFetcher.fetch() DOES decode Content-Encoding (calls _decode(raw.body, headers['content-encoding'], ...)). Only the robots path is affected. content-encoding is already in _SAFE_HEADERS, so RawHttpResponse.headers carries it; robots.py simply ignores it.
root_cause.reproduction: GET https://903hvac.com/robots.txt with Accept-Encoding: gzip returns HTTP 200, Content-Encoding: gzip, Transfer-Encoding: chunked, RAW body 872 bytes, RAW sha256 ef506dc1b57fb487ccdf3c54f676f7cf9fa5a3a356c559e8d7f1ea6402f12607 (byte-identical to the run's robots_evidence). gzip.decompress -> 1902 bytes containing 'User-agent: *' / 'Content-Signal: search=yes,ai-train=no,use=reference' / 'Allow: /'. raw.decode('utf-8','strict') raises UnicodeDecodeError: invalid start byte 0x8b at position 1 (gzip magic 1f 8b).
root_cause.policy_impact: 903hvac.com's actual robots.txt explicitly Allow: / for User-agent: *. Our RobotFileParser.can_fetch('OpportunityIntelligenceResearch', 'https://903hvac.com/') on the decompressed file returns True. The bounded M1 GET of / SHOULD have been permitted under the existing M1 robots policy; it was blocked solely by the undecoded-gzip defect.
root_cause.not_prohibited: Fixing this does not bypass robots (we still parse and obey Disallow, e.g. Amazonbot Disallow: /), does not bypass Cloudflare/bot-protection (gzip is a standard HTTP content coding, not a challenge), does not spoof a browser, does not broaden redirects, does not weaken TLS/SSRF/DNS-rebinding controls, and does not raise any request ceiling.
